# Rollout Plan: Migration of 40,000 Users from Legacy Billing System to New Billing System

## Overview

This plan migrates 40,000 existing users from the old billing system to the new billing system in three named phases. Because both systems can run concurrently, migrated and non-migrated users can be served simultaneously, allowing for controlled, reversible batches rather than a single cutover.

---

## Phase 1: Canary (2% of users, ~800 users)

**Entry criterion:** New billing system has passed a full end-to-end test suite in staging (invoicing, payment capture, refunds, proration, tax calculation) with 100% of test cases passing, and a rollback procedure has been documented and dry-run tested at least once.

**Scope:** Internal accounts and opted-in low-risk external users (e.g., monthly-cycle, single-currency, no active disputes or complex contracts).

**Activities:**
- Migrate accounts in small batches (e.g., 100 at a time) with manual verification of the first few batches.
- Run both systems in parallel per account for one full billing cycle; do not disable old-system billing for any migrated account until reconciliation passes.
- Compare invoices, charges, and balances line-by-line between old and new systems for every canary account.

**Exit criterion:** Reconciliation mismatch rate < 0.1% across the canary population for two consecutive billing cycles, and no unresolved Sev-1/Sev-2 incidents.

---

## Phase 2: Expansion (25% of users, ~10,000 users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 1 exit criteria met, sign-off from Billing Engineering, Finance, and Customer Support leads, and support ticket volume attributable to migration in Phase 1 is below 1% of migrated accounts.

**Scope:** Broader mix of user segments, including multiple currencies, annual contracts, and users with active discounts/coupons — but still excluding the highest-complexity accounts (e.g., enterprise custom contracts).

**Activities:**
- Migrate in daily or weekly waves (e.g., 1,000–2,000 users per wave) rather than all at once.
- Keep old system live in parallel (read/reconcile mode) for at least one full billing cycle per migrated wave before considering that wave "settled."
- Expand automated reconciliation tooling to run continuously, not just spot-checks.
- Support team staffed with a dedicated migration escalation queue.

**Exit criterion:** Reconciliation mismatch rate remains < 0.1%, payment failure rate for migrated users is within 0.5 percentage points of the old system's baseline failure rate, and no more than 2 Sev-1 incidents occurred during the phase.

---

## Phase 3: Full Migration (remaining ~73%, ~29,200 users, cumulative 100%)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 2 exit criteria met, all remaining edge-case account types (enterprise contracts, multi-entity billing, legacy pricing tiers) have been explicitly tested in staging or in a small Phase 2 sub-wave, and Finance has approved close-out procedures for the old system's ledger.

**Scope:** All remaining users, including the most complex account types, migrated last.

**Activities:**
- Migrate remaining users in waves sized to support capacity (e.g., 5,000–10,000 per wave).
- Continue parallel-run reconciliation for at least one full billing cycle after the final batch is migrated.
- Old billing system remains live, read-accessible, and able to reprocess/refund during this phase — no deletion, disabling, or decommissioning occurs while any batch of user migration is still in progress or has not completed its full parallel-run reconciliation window.

**Exit criterion:** All 40,000 users fully migrated, reconciliation mismatch rate < 0.1% sustained for two consecutive billing cycles after the last batch, zero unresolved Sev-1 incidents.

**Note:** Decommissioning of the old billing system is explicitly a separate, subsequent phase (Phase 4, not covered by this rollout plan), beginning only after Phase 3's exit criteria are fully met and a data-retention/audit sign-off is obtained. It never overlaps with the final batch of user migration.

---

## Halt Condition (Automatic)

The rollout must be automatically halted and no further users migrated to the next batch/phase if, at any point:

- **Reconciliation mismatch rate exceeds 0.5%** of migrated accounts in any 24-hour window, OR
- **Payment failure rate for migrated users exceeds the pre-migration baseline by more than 2 percentage points** in any 24-hour window.

Any halt triggers an immediate root-cause investigation before resuming; already-migrated users are not automatically rolled back, but new migrations pause until the issue is resolved.

---

## Risks

RISK: Duplicate or double-billing occurs when both systems attempt to charge the same account during the parallel-run window | Implement a mutual-exclusion flag per account so only one system is authoritative for actual charge execution while the other runs in shadow/reconciliation-only mode | Billing Engineering Lead
RISK: Data mapping errors (e.g., incorrect proration, tax rates, or currency conversion) cause incorrect invoice amounts for migrated users | Run automated line-by-line reconciliation between old and new system outputs for every migrated account before disabling old-system charging for that account | Data Migration Engineer
RISK: Customer support is overwhelmed by billing disputes from confused or incorrectly charged migrated users | Pre-train support staff on the new system, staff a dedicated migration escalation queue, and throttle batch size based on real-time ticket volume | Customer Support Manager
RISK: Rollback of a migrated batch is not actually possible once account state has diverged between systems | Require a tested, documented rollback runbook and a maximum "point of no return" defined per batch before that batch is approved to migrate | Site Reliability Engineering Lead

---

PHASES: 3
